title: Jack Grealish returns to the pitch for Everton and becomes a standout
seoTitle: Jack Grealish returns for Everton and shines
subtitle: Off‑offensive midfielder reappeared in a match against Manchester United, on loan to the club, and already shows potential.
excerpt: Jack Grealish made his Everton debut on loan against Manchester United. His return sparked excitement and impact, but manager Moyes stresses his physical condition.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: The Guardian, Read Everton, Everton News
contentHtml:
The presence of Jack Grealish on the field for Everton, in his loan debut against Manchester United, is why the offensive midfielder’s name is trending. The player, who came on in the second half, instantly displayed his potential, creating dangerous chances and energising the side.

Gre​alish’s return to Everton

Jack Grealish made his return to the pitch after being re‑loaned to Everton, taking the field against Manchester United. With 25 minutes left, the attacking midfielder was greeted with enthusiasm by the Everton crowd. He is described as universally popular because of his desire to entertain, and his entrance quickly revived the hosts, generating dangerous situations within seconds.

In the match against Manchester United, which ended in a dramatic draw with goals from Ainsley Maitland‑Niles and Tyrique George, Grealish replaced Brennan Johnson in the 66th minute. This was his second debut for the Toffees, and he impressed coming off the bench.

Manager David Moyes on the player’s fitness

Everton manager David Moyes commented on Grealish’s physical condition after the game. Moyes praised the player’s ability to keep possession and deliver precise passes. However, the coach admitted that Grealish still needs to improve his fitness, having played little over the past six months due to a foot injury.

Moyes said Grealish “has not had minutes… when you look at his minutes, he had a few short spells with Manchester City, but nothing really. He hasn’t played for six and a half months.” The goal is for Grealish to reach a level of readiness to play longer and be more prepared for upcoming matches.

The role of Grealish in the team and expectations

For David Moyes, if Everton wants to fight for a top‑half spot, Grealish will be needed as a creative focal point. For now, the 30‑year‑old midfielder will likely be used as an impact substitute. Moyes does not expect him to start games immediately, given his need to regain full fitness.

Gre​alish’s situation has already created a “selection dilemma” for Moyes, with Brennan Johnson and Tyrique George among his other options on the flanks. Tyrique George, in particular, is expected to start on the left wing against Tottenham Hotspur this weekend. Tyler Dibling is another option, but appears to be the second choice and has had limited minutes.

Everton’s moment in the Premier League

Everton have shown a solid start to the Premier League season, accumulating five points from three games and remaining unbeaten. After the match against Manchester United, the side secured a dramatic point, with Maitland‑Niles scoring an impressive goal on his debut and Tyrique George netting his first for the club.

Despite a few challenges, the club finds itself in a better position than expected, especially after the turbulence surrounding the transfer‑window deadline. Christian Nørgaard is the only confirmed senior absentee for Everton at the moment.
